source_meta._title: Riptide tridents use mainhand item to inflict damage when thrown in the offhand

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.13 in a fresh single-player world using the integrated server. Use a Superflat world for a level test area, enable cheats, begin in Creative mode for deterministic construction and item acquisition, and switch to Survival mode before performing the damage trials. Use an unmodified vanilla client with no datapacks, attribute modifiers, or status effects beyond those created by the described setup.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher has an installation profile for the exact release Minecraft 1.13; do not substitute 1.13.1 or a later version.
Create a fresh single-player Superflat world with Game Mode set to Creative and Allow Cheats enabled.
Use one player only. The player should have no Strength effect or other effect that changes attack damage.
Default keyboard and mouse inputs are assumed. If controls are rebound, use the mapped controls for Open Chat, Inventory, Use Item, and Swap Item With Offhand.
The Damage scoreboard objective must not already exist. A fresh world satisfies this condition.
The test lane must provide water at its launch end because a Riptide trident can launch its user only while the user is in water or exposed to rain.
Use two ordinary, unarmored sheep: one for the mainhand control trial and a fresh one for the offhand trigger trial.

steps.action: Launch the exact Minecraft Java Edition profile named Minecraft 1.13. Create and enter a fresh Creative-mode Superflat world with cheats enabled. Wait until the terrain has rendered and movement and inventory input respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The F3 version text, title screen version label, or launcher profile confirms Minecraft 1.13, and the player is standing in a loaded Superflat world in Creative mode.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory using the Inventory control, default E. Obtain one Trident, at least two Sheep Spawn Eggs, one Water Bucket, and enough solid blocks to build a short test corridor. Put the trident, sheep spawn eggs, and water bucket in separate hotbar slots.
steps.success_cue: The hotbar contains a Trident, at least two Sheep Spawn Eggs, and a Water Bucket; solid building blocks are also available.

steps.action: Construct a straight test lane on the flat ground. Make its interior one block wide and at least ten blocks long. Place solid sidewalls two blocks high along both sides and cap the far end with a solid wall. Keep the near end open. This confines each sheep to the player's forward Riptide path without putting a barrier between the player and sheep.
steps.success_cue: A straight, one-block-wide corridor at least ten blocks long is open at the near end, closed at the far end, and has two-block-high sidewalls.

steps.action: At the open end of the corridor, remove the first two floor blocks to form a one-block-deep, two-block-long trench. Use the Water Bucket to fill both trench blocks with stationary water source blocks. Riptide requires the user to be in water or rain when activating it. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3AAchievement_guide?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: Right-click / Use Item with Water Bucket
steps.success_cue: The corridor begins with a two-block-long water trench in which the player can stand, and the remaining lane ahead has a solid floor.

steps.action: Select the Trident's hotbar slot so that the trident is visibly held in the main hand.
steps.exact_input: Press the number key assigned to the Trident's hotbar slot
steps.success_cue: A Trident is visible in the player's main hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Enter the exact enchantment command, including the leading slash, and press Enter. The selected mainhand item must remain the Trident while executing the command. The /enchant command and resource-location enchantment argument are available in Java Edition 1.13. ([pt.minecraft.wiki](https://pt.minecraft.wiki/w/Comandos/enchant?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The command reports that the enchantment was applied. Hovering over the Trident in the inventory shows Riptide I.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Enter the report's first scoreboard command exactly, including the leading slash, and press Enter. Cheats are required because this is an in-game command.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that the Damage objective was created successfully.

steps.action: Press T, enter the report's sidebar-display command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The Damage objective is assigned to the right-side scoreboard display; it may remain empty until the player's score is initialized.

steps.action: Press T, enter the report's player-initialization command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The right-side Damage sidebar displays the current player's name with an initialized numerical score.

steps.action: Switch to Survival mode for the two damage trials. Press T, enter the command with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The Survival health and hunger bars are visible, and chat confirms that the player's game mode was changed to Survival.

steps.action: Select a Sheep Spawn Egg. Enter the corridor and right-click the solid floor approximately three to five blocks beyond the water trench to spawn the first sheep. Immediately move back toward the water end so the sheep remains ahead of the player in the corridor.
steps.exact_input: Right-click / Use Item with Sheep Spawn Egg
steps.success_cue: One ordinary sheep is alive inside the narrow corridor, with no solid barrier between it and the water launch area.

steps.action: Select the Riptide I Trident's hotbar slot again. Stand inside the water trench, face directly down the corridor, and place the crosshair on the first sheep's body. Ensure the Trident is still in the main hand.
steps.exact_input: Select Trident hotbar slot; use mouse movement to aim
steps.success_cue: The player's feet or body are in water, the Riptide I Trident is in the main hand, and the first sheep is directly ahead under the crosshair.

steps.action: Press and hold Use Item, default right mouse button, while remaining in the water and keeping the crosshair aligned with the sheep. Hold until the Trident has completed its charge animation; do not release early.
steps.exact_input: Hold Right Mouse Button / Use Item
steps.success_cue: The mainhand Riptide I Trident is fully charged while the player remains in water and aimed down the corridor.

steps.action: Release Use Item to activate the mainhand Riptide launch. Do not steer sideways or make a separate left-click attack. Allow the propelled player to collide once with the first sheep, then release movement and attack controls.
steps.exact_input: Release Right Mouse Button / Use Item
steps.success_cue: The mainhand Riptide movement and a single collision with the first sheep have completed, and no follow-up attack has been made.

steps.action: Wait until Riptide movement has ended and the Damage sidebar has stopped changing. Record the numerical Damage score shown after this mainhand control collision, but do not alter or reset it. This recorded value is the baseline from which the second collision's increase can be calculated.
steps.success_cue: The post-control Damage score has been recorded, the sidebar remains visible, and the player is stationary.

steps.action: Select the Sheep Spawn Egg and spawn a fresh second sheep on the corridor floor. If the first sheep survived, keep the second sheep spatially distinct and target only the fresh sheep; if necessary, wait until the first sheep is away from the intended collision line. Do not attack either sheep manually.
steps.exact_input: Right-click / Use Item with Sheep Spawn Egg
steps.success_cue: A fresh, unarmored second sheep is alive in the corridor and can be used as the offhand trial target.

steps.action: Return to the water trench at the open end of the corridor. Face the fresh second sheep and ensure no other entity is closer along the launch path.
steps.success_cue: The player is back at the water launch end, and the second sheep is the first entity directly ahead in the corridor.

steps.action: Select the Riptide I Trident in the main hand, then use Swap Item With Offhand, default F, once. This moves the Trident into the offhand and moves the previously empty offhand contents into the selected mainhand hotbar slot. If the offhand was not empty, instead open the inventory with E, clear the shield-shaped offhand slot, and drag the Trident into that slot. Tridents can be equipped and used from the offhand. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Dual_wield?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The Riptide I Trident is visibly held in the offhand, and the currently selected mainhand hotbar slot is completely empty.

steps.action: Stand in the water trench and aim the crosshair directly at the fresh second sheep. Reconfirm that the main hand is visually empty and that the Riptide I Trident remains in the offhand. Do not select another hotbar item.
steps.success_cue: The player is wet, the main hand is empty, the Riptide I Trident is in the offhand, and the second sheep is directly ahead under the crosshair.

steps.action: Record the current Damage sidebar value immediately before charging the offhand Trident. Do not reset the objective and do not perform any attack between recording this value and activating Riptide.
steps.success_cue: The exact pre-collision Damage value for the offhand trial has been recorded and remains unchanged.

steps.action: Press and hold Use Item, default right mouse button. Because the selected mainhand slot is empty, the offhand Riptide I Trident should begin charging. Remain in the water and keep the crosshair aligned with the second sheep until charging is complete.
steps.exact_input: Hold Right Mouse Button / Use Item
steps.success_cue: The offhand Riptide I Trident is fully charged while the player remains in water, the main hand remains empty, and the second sheep is aligned with the launch path.

steps.action: Release Use Item to activate the offhand Riptide launch. Do not left-click, change hotbar slots, or steer sideways. Allow the propelled player to collide exactly once with the fresh second sheep, then make no further attack or item-use inputs.
steps.exact_input: Release Right Mouse Button / Use Item
steps.success_cue: The offhand Riptide launch has produced one completed player-to-sheep collision, the Damage sidebar remains visible, and no additional attack has occurred.

stor.handoff_condition: The player, with an empty main hand and the Riptide I Trident still in the offhand, has just completed exactly one Riptide-propelled collision with the fresh second sheep. The Damage sidebar is still visible, the immediately preceding score was recorded at step 20, and no further attack, item use, hotbar change, or scoreboard command has been performed. Begin observation now.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a world type, game mode, or single-player versus server environment. A fresh single-player Superflat world, Creative setup, and Survival execution are practical deterministic choices rather than report requirements.
The description says to spawn an entity, while the more detailed confirming comment specifies a sheep. This plan uses sheep to match that detailed reproduction.

The report describes one spawned entity but the mainhand control strike can kill an ordinary sheep. This plan uses one fresh sheep per trial so both strikes have valid, undamaged targets; that is a practical execution inference.

The report omits the wetness condition needed to activate Riptide. The water launch trench was added after external verification that Riptide launches only while the player is in water or exposed to rain. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3AAchievement_guide?utm_source=openai))

The affected-version metadata includes 24w19a and 24w20a even though 24w19a is also listed as the fix version and the final comment states that the reporter could not reproduce in either version. All affected-version strings were nevertheless preserved exactly as supplied, and Minecraft 1.13 remains the recommended version because it is the first listed affected version.

The exact scoreboard increases described by the report are intentionally not included as success cues or handoff criteria because evaluating those values belongs to the separate observation subsystem.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:inward:MC-4708:Explosion deals no damage to the player in "Peaceful" difficulty | Duplicate:inward:MC-258817:1.19.3 protection causing ender crystal damage reduce more under hard mode | Duplicate:inward:MC-259072:End Crystals deal less damage on hard mode | Relates:outward:MC-258561:Endermen teleport away instead of taking damage from end crystal, TNT and wither skull explosions | Relates:inward:MC-260993:End crystals and TNT explosions do same damage regardless of difficulty for entities except players
source_meta._title: End crystal and TNT explosions do same damage regardless of difficulty

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition 1.19.3 in a disposable single-player Superflat world using the integrated server. Cheats are enabled. Creative mode is used only for setup; the explosion is triggered in Survival mode on Peaceful difficulty. Natural health regeneration is disabled, the player has 200 maximum health, and the player has no armor, shield, protective status effects, or other equipment.
preconditions: Install and select the exact Java Edition version 1.19.3 in the Minecraft Launcher; do not use the fix version 23w06a or a later version for this reproduction.
Use an unmodified vanilla client without mods, plugins, or datapacks that alter explosions, damage, difficulty, health, armor, attributes, or status effects.
Use a disposable world because the end crystal explosion can damage terrain outside the protected test pad.

Keyboard and mouse controls must permit opening chat, looking around, and performing the Attack/Destroy action. The default chat key is T and the default Attack/Destroy input is the left mouse button.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select and launch the exact installation for Java Edition 1.19.3. From the title screen, select Singleplayer.
steps.success_cue: The lower-left corner of the title screen identifies the running version as Minecraft 1.19.3, and the Singleplayer world-selection screen is open.

steps.action: Select Create New World. Set Game Mode to Creative and set Allow Cheats to ON. Open More World Options, cycle World Type until Superflat is selected, return to the main creation screen, and select Create New World. No particular seed is required.
steps.success_cue: A new Superflat world has loaded, the player can fly, and commands are available.

steps.action: Land on the flat surface in an open area, away from any generated village or other entities. Stop moving and wait until the surrounding terrain is rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing still on unobstructed flat ground and nearby chunks are fully rendered.

steps.action: Create an explosion-resistant test pad directly beneath and around the player. Press T to open chat, enter the exact command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: An 11-by-11 obsidian pad is visible at the player's feet, with the player standing near its center.

steps.action: Disable natural health regeneration so Peaceful-mode healing cannot change the player's health immediately after the explosion. Press T, enter the exact command, and press Enter. This game rule controls natural health regeneration, including Peaceful regeneration. ([zh.minecraft.wiki](https://zh.minecraft.wiki/w/%E7%8E%A9%E5%AE%B6?variant=zh-tw&utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: Chat reports that the naturalRegeneration game rule is now false.

steps.action: Set the report-supported non-Normal test difficulty to Peaceful. Press T, enter the exact command, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that the difficulty has been set to Peaceful.

steps.action: Increase the player's base maximum health so one point-blank end crystal explosion can be measured without ending the test through player death. Press T, enter the exact command, and press Enter. The generic.max_health attribute identifier and attribute command are available in this affected-version command format. ([zh.minecraft.wiki](https://zh.minecraft.wiki/w/Java%E7%89%881.16/%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%91%E7%89%88%E6%9C%AC?variant=zh-tw&utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted and reports that the player's minecraft:generic.max_health base value was set to 200.

steps.action: Remove all inventory, hotbar, armor-slot, and offhand items so armor, enchantments, a shield, or another held item cannot affect the test. Press T, enter the exact command, and press Enter. A response saying that no items were found is also acceptable because the required empty state is already satisfied.
steps.success_cue: The hotbar is empty, and the player has no equipped armor or offhand item.

steps.action: Remove any active status effects before applying the setup heal. Press T, enter the exact command, and press Enter. A response saying that no effects could be removed is acceptable because it confirms that no effects were active.
steps.success_cue: No status-effect icons are present and no protective effect remains active.

steps.action: Fill the enlarged health pool using Instant Health. Press T, enter the exact command, and press Enter. Java Edition's effect command accepts the target, effect identifier, duration, amplifier, and hide-particles arguments in this order. ([zh.minecraft.wiki](https://zh.minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3A%E7%94%A8%E5%91%BD%E4%BB%A4%E6%93%8D%E6%8E%A7%E5%AE%9E%E4%BD%93?variant=zh-hk&utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The Instant Health command is accepted; the enlarged health pool is ready to be checked after entering Survival mode.

steps.action: Switch to Survival mode so the player can receive explosion damage. Press T, enter the exact command, and press Enter. Do not equip any items afterward.
steps.success_cue: The health and hunger HUDs are visible, multiple rows of hearts are full, no armor icons are displayed, and the hotbar remains empty.

steps.action: While standing still near the center of the obsidian pad, summon the end crystal at the player's exact current coordinates. Press T, enter the exact command including the leading slash, and press Enter. Do not walk away after executing it. The summon command accepts an entity identifier followed by coordinates, and an end crystal summoned without extra NBT is a valid entity. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/minecraft-commands?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: One rotating end crystal is visible overlapping the player's position on the obsidian pad, and the player has not moved away from it.

steps.action: Without moving from the crystal's position, turn only as much as necessary to place the crosshair on the crystal's rotating central model. With an empty main hand and no shield, press the Attack/Destroy control once—left mouse button by default—to strike and destroy the crystal. End crystals detonate when hit. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3ADefeating_the_ender_dragon?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The end crystal has been struck, the crystal entity is gone, and its explosion has just completed. Do not move, heal, change difficulty, or execute another command before handoff.

stor.handoff_condition: The unarmored player is in Survival mode on Peaceful difficulty with naturalRegeneration disabled and a 200-point maximum-health pool, and has just detonated an overlapping end crystal while standing on the center of the obsidian test pad. Begin observing the player's post-explosion health immediately, before any further input or state change.
uncertainties: The report permits Hard, Peaceful, or Easy but does not require one specific non-Normal difficulty. Peaceful is selected as the simplest deterministic variant.

The report does not specify a world seed, world type, game mode, armor state, health capacity, regeneration setting, or exact crystal-spawning method. The Superflat world, obsidian pad, temporary Creative setup, Survival trigger state, empty equipment, 200 maximum health, and disabled natural regeneration are practical controls added to make a single explosion survivable and measurable without changing its difficulty setting.
The report says to spawn an end crystal but supplies no command. The plan uses the version-compatible command /summon minecraft:end_crystal ~ ~ ~ to place it at the player's current position.
TNT is mentioned in the title and description, but the report's formal reproduction steps use an end crystal. This plan reproduces only the end-crystal path and does not add a separate TNT variant.

The report does not state whether 'stand in the middle' means an exact entity-coordinate overlap. Summoning the crystal at ~ ~ ~ while the player remains stationary is used as the deterministic interpretation.

source_meta._title: Less recent attacker can be credited for kill

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition 1.19.4 Release Candidate 2, identified as 1.19.4-rc2 in the launcher; fresh single-player Superflat Overworld using the integrated server; Creative mode with commands enabled for setup, followed by Survival mode on Easy difficulty for the attack sequence. Natural mob spawning is disabled and time is frozen at midnight to isolate the Zombie and Husk. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/minecraft-1-19-4-release-candidate-1?utm_source=openai))
preconditions: Install and launch the exact affected version 1.19.4 Release Candidate 2, not the fixed version 1.20 Pre-release 3.
Use a fresh disposable world so testing a historical release candidate cannot affect an important world.
Commands/cheats must be enabled because the plan uses commands to create a deterministic test arena and concludes with the report-provided /kill command.
Use one player in single-player. No dedicated server or second player is required by the report.
Begin the attack sequence at full health in Survival mode, without a shield raised and without armor or status effects that obscure whether damage was received.
Do not strike or kill either test mob. The player must receive melee damage first from the Zombie and then from the Husk.
No damage source other than the designated Zombie, designated Husk, and final /kill command may affect the player during the timed sequence.

Complete the sequence from the Zombie hit through submission of /kill in less than five seconds. If the Husk hits first, another entity deals damage, or the order cannot be confirmed, abandon that attempt and repeat the setup before handing off.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, enable historical snapshot/release-candidate installations if necessary, create or select an installation using version 1.19.4-rc2, and launch it. Do not select 1.19.4-rc1, another release candidate, or a fix version. The launcher identifier for the report's first affected version is 1.19.4-rc2. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/minecraft-1-19-4-release-candidate-1?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The title screen is open in Minecraft: Java Edition 1.19.4 Release Candidate 2.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, then Create New World. On the Game tab, set Game Mode to Creative, Difficulty to Easy, and Allow Cheats to ON. On the World tab, select Superflat as the world type. Leave experiments and data packs disabled, then create the world. The affected version's world-creation screen exposes game mode, difficulty, cheats, and world type through these tabs. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/minecraft-java-edition-1-19-4?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: A new Creative-mode Superflat world begins loading with commands enabled.

steps.action: Wait without entering commands until the terrain around the player has rendered and movement responds normally. Move to a flat, unobstructed patch with at least eight blocks of clear horizontal space, then stop moving. Remain at this same position while running the relative-position summon commands.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary on level ground with a clear area in front and to either side, and nearby chunks are fully responsive.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat, enter the difficulty command including the leading slash, and press Enter. This explicitly prevents Peaceful difficulty from removing the hostile test mobs.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback confirms that the difficulty is Easy.

steps.action: Press T, enter the following command including the leading slash, and press Enter. This prevents unrelated mobs from naturally spawning during the isolated test. Java Edition gamerules use the form /gamerule <rule> <value>. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Commands/gamerule?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: Command feedback confirms that doMobSpawning is set to false.

steps.action: Press T, enter the following command including the leading slash, and press Enter to stop the day/night cycle.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback confirms that doDaylightCycle is set to false.

steps.action: Press T, enter the following command including the leading slash, and press Enter. Freezing the world at midnight prevents the Zombie and Husk from burning before the test is completed.
steps.success_cue: The sky is dark and remains at night because the daylight cycle is disabled.

steps.action: While still in Creative mode, press T, enter the following command including the leading slash, and press Enter. This removes any already-loaded non-player entities so that only the two subsequently summoned attackers can participate.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback reports that loaded non-player entities were killed, and no nearby mobs remain.

steps.action: Return to the stationary setup position if the previous actions caused any movement. Face any convenient direction and do not move until both summon commands and both Slowness commands have been completed; the summon coordinates are relative to the player's current position.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary on the flat test surface with at least eight clear blocks around the intended mob positions.

steps.action: Press T, enter the following command including the leading slash, and press Enter. It summons one adult persistent Zombie three blocks along positive Z from the stationary player. Java Edition /summon accepts an entity identifier, position, and optional NBT. ([zh.minecraft.wiki](https://zh.minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3A%E7%94%A8%E5%91%BD%E4%BB%A4%E6%93%8D%E6%8E%A7%E5%AE%9E%E4%BD%93?variant=zh-hk&utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: One adult green-skinned Zombie is visible approximately three blocks from the player.

steps.action: Without moving from the setup position, press T, enter the following command including the leading slash, and press Enter. The extreme Slowness effect keeps the Zombie near its assigned position while retaining its ability to perform a melee attack when the player enters reach.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback confirms that Slowness was applied to the nearest Zombie, and the Zombie remains nearly or completely stationary.

steps.action: Still without moving, press T, enter the following command including the leading slash, and press Enter. It summons one adult persistent Husk five blocks along positive X and three blocks along positive Z from the setup position, separating it from the Zombie while keeping the distance short enough for the timed sequence.
steps.success_cue: One adult tan/brown Husk is visible about five blocks to the side of the Zombie; both designated attackers are present and visually distinguishable.

steps.action: Without moving, press T, enter the following command including the leading slash, and press Enter. This keeps the Husk at its assigned position until the player deliberately approaches it.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback confirms that Slowness was applied to the nearest Husk, and both attackers remain separated and stationary.

steps.action: Confirm that the health bar will be easy to monitor and that no shield is raised. Press T, enter the following command including the leading slash, and press Enter to change only the executing player to Survival mode. Omitting a player argument targets the player executing /gamemode. ([es.minecraft.wiki](https://es.minecraft.wiki/w/Comandos/gamemode?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: Hearts and hunger are visible above the hotbar, the player can receive damage, and the stationary Zombie and Husk begin targeting the player.

steps.action: Approach only the green Zombie until it performs exactly one melee attack. Do not attack, block, open a menu, or allow the Husk into melee range. The instant the Zombie's hit is confirmed, begin the five-second timed portion of the reproduction.
steps.success_cue: The player has just received one damage event from the Zombie, confirmed by a health decrease, hurt sound, red damage flash, or knockback; the Husk has not yet hit the player.

steps.action: Immediately sprint out of the Zombie's melee reach and directly toward the separated tan/brown Husk. Use the Sprint action, Left Ctrl by default, while holding the appropriate movement key. Do not pause, and do not pass back through the Zombie's reach.
steps.success_cue: The Zombie is behind and outside melee reach, while the player is approaching the Husk within the same five-second window.

steps.action: Enter the Husk's melee reach and allow the Husk to perform exactly one melee attack. Do not strike or block against it. Confirm the damage event before proceeding.
steps.success_cue: The player has received a Zombie melee hit followed by a more recent Husk melee hit, in that exact order, with no intervening damage source.

steps.action: Immediately move approximately three blocks away from the immobilized Husk so it cannot deliver another attack while chat is being opened. Continue treating the five-second limit as running from the Zombie's hit.
steps.success_cue: Both mobs are outside immediate melee reach, the player is still alive, and the most recent damage event was the Husk's hit.

steps.action: Before five seconds have elapsed since the Zombie hit, press T to open in-game chat, type the report-provided command exactly with its leading slash, and press Enter once. In Java Edition, /kill with no target argument targets the entity executing the command, which here is the player. Do not inspect or interpret the resulting killer attribution; hand control to the observation subsystem immediately. ([zh.minecraft.wiki](https://zh.minecraft.wiki/w/%E5%91%BD%E4%BB%A4/kill?variant=zh&utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The /kill command has been submitted by the player immediately after the Zombie-then-Husk damage sequence, and the game has transitioned to the player's death state.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just submitted /kill after receiving one Zombie melee hit followed by one Husk melee hit, with the entire sequence from the Zombie hit through command submission completed within five seconds and with no other damage source intervening. The death screen and associated text are now available for the separate Observation Agent; take no further player action.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a seed, coordinates, world type, game mode, difficulty, single-player versus dedicated server, or how to obtain the Zombie and Husk. A fresh single-player Superflat world, Creative command-based setup, and Easy Survival trigger phase are practical choices intended to remove exploration and random spawning.

The report's comment mentions a five-second attacker-memory limit but does not unambiguously state whether the interval is measured from the first hit, the most recent hit, or another internal event. This plan conservatively completes the entire Zombie-hit-to-/kill sequence within five seconds.
Version 1.19.3 is mentioned in a comment but is not present in the formal Affects versions field, so it is intentionally excluded from affected_versions.

The high-level report only requires one Zombie hit followed by one Husk hit. The Slowness effects, disabled natural spawning, frozen midnight, mob separation, and entity cleanup are deterministic execution aids rather than asserted bug requirements.

The generic command and UI details were checked against permitted Minecraft.net and Minecraft Wiki sources, but the supplied Mojira report remains the source of truth for the attacker order and exact /kill trigger.

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.21 Pre-Release 3 in a new, unmodified singleplayer world. Use Creative mode with commands/cheats available for deterministic setup, then change to Survival mode before the triggering attack. Use keyboard and mouse controls; the listed keys assume default bindings.
preconditions: Launch the exact affected version listed as Minecraft Java Edition 1.21 Pre-Release 3, not a later release or either listed fix version.
Create a disposable singleplayer world in Creative mode with commands available. A flat preset is optional but can make entity placement easier.
Use an open, level area with a solid block beneath the player and enough room for an allay and a cow.
Do not install mods or datapacks that alter combat, allay behavior, enchantments, entity immunity, or attack cooldowns.
The player must be standing on the ground, not sprinting, not jumping, and must allow the sword attack cooldown to become fully charged before the trigger.
The commands below must be entered in in-game chat with the leading slash. If command feedback reports insufficient permission, recreate the world with commands enabled.
After selecting the setup position, avoid walking away from it: the entity summon coordinates are relative to the player's position.

steps.action: Load the new world using Minecraft Java Edition 1.21 Pre-Release 3 and wait for world initialization to finish.
steps.success_cue: The player can move normally, nearby terrain is rendered, and the pause menu identifies the running version as 1.21 Pre-Release 3.

steps.action: Move to an open, level area, stand on a solid block, and stop moving. Remain at this position through the setup so the relative summon coordinates stay usable.
steps.exact_input: W/A/S/D as needed, then release all movement keys
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary on level ground with at least three blocks of unobstructed space nearby.

steps.action: Summon a stationary allay slightly more than two blocks from the player. Press T to open in-game chat, enter the exact command including the leading slash, and press Enter. The NoAI tag is used only to prevent the allay from leaving the controlled test position.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback indicates that an allay was summoned, and one allay is visible approximately two blocks from the player.

steps.action: Obtain one cobblestone item to assign the allay to the player. Open in-game chat, execute the exact command, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A cobblestone item is present in the player's inventory or hotbar, and command feedback reports that the item was given.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the cobblestone. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the screen; use the corresponding number key or the mouse wheel until that slot has the selection outline.
steps.exact_input: Hotbar number key 1-9 or mouse wheel
steps.success_cue: Cobblestone is visible in the player's main hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair directly at the summoned allay and use the item on it once to give it the cobblestone. With default controls, use means right-click.
steps.success_cue: The cobblestone leaves the player's hand and is visibly held by the allay, establishing that the allay has been assigned to this player.

steps.action: Without changing the player's position, summon a stationary cow as the primary attack target. Open in-game chat, execute the exact command, and press Enter. The cow will be placed next to the assigned allay so the allay is within the sword's sweeping area.
steps.success_cue: A cow is visible approximately two blocks from the player, with the item-holding allay immediately beside it.

steps.action: Obtain a diamond sword. Open in-game chat, execute the exact command, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A diamond sword is present in the player's inventory or hotbar, and command feedback reports that the item was given.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the diamond sword by pressing that slot's number key or using the mouse wheel.
steps.exact_input: Hotbar number key 1-9 or mouse wheel
steps.success_cue: The diamond sword is visible in the player's main hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: While the diamond sword remains selected in the main hand, apply Fire Aspect I. Press T, enter the exact enchant command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback reports that Fire Aspect was applied to the selected sword; the sword remains selected and has the enchanted-item glint.

steps.action: Change the player to Survival mode for the combat action. Open in-game chat, execute the exact command, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback reports that the game mode was set to Survival, and the health and hunger bars are visible above the hotbar.

steps.action: Without pressing movement, sprint, jump, or attack, rotate the camera until the crosshair is centered on the cow's body. Confirm visually that the cobblestone-holding allay remains immediately adjacent to the cow rather than between the crosshair and the cow.
steps.exact_input: Move mouse only; do not press W/A/S/D, Left Ctrl, Space, or left-click
steps.success_cue: The crosshair is on the cow, the adjacent allay still visibly holds cobblestone, and the player remains stationary on the ground.

steps.action: Keep the crosshair on the cow and wait at least one full second without attacking. This ensures the sword attack cooldown is fully charged so the next grounded, non-sprinting sword attack can produce a sweeping attack.
steps.exact_input: Wait at least 1 second with all attack and movement controls released
steps.success_cue: At least one second has elapsed since any attack, the player is still grounded and stationary, and the cow and assigned allay remain adjacent.

steps.action: Attack the cow exactly once with the fully cooled Fire Aspect sword while remaining grounded and stationary. With default controls, attack means left-click. Do not click a second time.
steps.success_cue: One sword attack input has been delivered to the cow while the assigned, item-holding allay is still within the sweeping area beside it.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just completed one fully cooled, grounded, non-sprinting attack against the cow with the Fire Aspect sword while the item-holding allay is immediately adjacent. Begin observation immediately after this single attack and do not perform another attack.
uncertainties: The report lists 24w33a both under affected versions and fix versions. The plan follows the required ordering rule and uses the first affected version, 1.21 Pre-Release 3.
The report does not specify a particular target mob; a cow is used as a deterministic, non-hostile implementation of the report's generic instruction to attack a mob.
The report does not require Sweeping Edge, so the plan adds only Fire Aspect I and relies on the normal fully charged sweeping attack performed by a grounded, non-sprinting player wielding a sword.
The NoAI entity tag and exact relative placement are deterministic setup aids inferred for automation; the report itself only requires an assigned allay to be within range of the sweeping effect.

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 25w41a in a new vanilla single-player test world, using keyboard and mouse. Use Creative mode with commands enabled for deterministic setup, then change to Survival mode before attacking. Use the default resource pack, no mods that alter combat or sound, and an audible or recordable game-audio output.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher can install and launch Java Edition snapshot 25w41a.
Use a disposable test world rather than an important existing world because snapshots can damage or alter saved worlds.
The client has no resource pack or mod that replaces attack sounds or changes melee-combat behavior.
Master Volume and gameplay/player sound volume are above 0, and the operating-system output or automated audio-capture channel is not muted.
Use the bound equivalents if inventory, chat, jump, attack, or use controls have been changed from their defaults.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, open Minecraft: Java Edition -> Installations, enable the Snapshots filter if necessary, and create or select an installation whose version is exactly 25w41a. Launch that installation. The official 25w41a page identifies it as a Java Edition snapshot and documents enabling snapshots from the Installations tab. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/minecraft-snapshot-25w41a?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: Minecraft Launcher -> Minecraft: Java Edition -> Installations -> Snapshots enabled -> version 25w41a -> Play
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu loads and displays version 25w41a on the screen.

steps.action: Create a new single-player test world in Creative mode. Keep commands enabled so the player can be changed to Survival mode after setup. Wait until terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Allow Commands: ON, if shown -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player is in a newly loaded Creative-mode world and can move normally.

steps.action: Ensure attack sounds can be heard or captured. Open the pause menu, enter the sound settings, set Master Volume and the Players sound category above 0, then return to the world. If an external audio recorder is used, verify that it is capturing Minecraft's output device.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Options -> Music & Sounds -> Master Volume above 0% and Players above 0% -> Done
steps.success_cue: Minecraft is unpaused, and ordinary interface or movement sounds are audible or visible in the audio-capture meter.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Open the Search Items tab, obtain one Block of Copper, one Carved Pumpkin, and one unenchanted Iron Sword, and place all three in separate hotbar slots. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the screen.
steps.exact_input: E; search for "Block of Copper", "Carved Pumpkin", and "Iron Sword"; move one of each to the hotbar
steps.success_cue: The hotbar contains a Block of Copper, a Carved Pumpkin, and an unenchanted Iron Sword.

steps.action: Close the inventory and move to a flat, solid location with at least a 3-by-3-block clear area and two unobstructed blocks of vertical space above the ground. Stop flying and stand on the ground before constructing the golem.
steps.exact_input: E to close inventory; use movement controls to reach a clear area; descend with the bound Sneak control, default Left Shift, if flying
steps.success_cue: The player is standing on solid flat ground with enough open space for a copper golem to appear.

steps.action: Select the Block of Copper in the hotbar and use it on the ground to place a single copper block.
steps.exact_input: Select the Block of Copper hotbar slot, then right-click the target ground position
steps.success_cue: One Block of Copper is present on the ground directly in front of the player, with the space above it empty.

steps.action: Select the Carved Pumpkin and right-click the top face of the placed Block of Copper. Placing a carved pumpkin directly atop a copper block is the officially documented method of summoning a copper golem. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/the-copper-cape-quest))
steps.exact_input: Select the Carved Pumpkin hotbar slot, aim at the top face of the Block of Copper, and right-click once
steps.success_cue: The two placed blocks convert into a living copper golem that is visible near the player.

steps.action: Select the unenchanted Iron Sword in the hotbar so it is held in the player's main hand. Do not attack yet.
steps.exact_input: Press the number key corresponding to the Iron Sword hotbar slot, or scroll to that slot
steps.success_cue: The Iron Sword is visible in the player's main hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Change from Creative mode to Survival mode. Press T to open chat, type the command exactly as shown with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds, the Survival health and hunger HUD is visible, and the player is no longer using Creative flight.

steps.action: Approach the copper golem on level ground until it is within normal melee reach, no more than approximately three blocks away. Keep the crosshair centered on the golem's body. Stop sprinting and ensure the player is not in water, climbing, riding another entity, or otherwise prevented from performing a normal jump critical attack.
steps.exact_input: Use movement controls to approach; release movement and sprint controls; aim the crosshair at the copper golem
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary on solid ground within melee reach, with the crosshair continuously aimed at the copper golem.

steps.action: Without pressing the attack control, wait at least two seconds so the Iron Sword's attack cooldown is fully charged. If an attack-strength indicator is enabled, wait until it is completely filled. Java Edition melee attacks use a cooldown, and attacking before it refills produces a reduced-strength attack. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3ABeginner%27s_guide?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: Wait at least 2 seconds without left-clicking
steps.success_cue: At least two seconds have elapsed since any attack input, and the attack-strength indicator is full if it is displayed.

steps.action: While still aimed at the copper golem and without sprinting, press the Jump control once. Allow the player to pass the top of the jump and begin moving downward. Do not press the attack control while still rising.
steps.exact_input: Press Space once, then wait until the player has passed the jump apex
steps.success_cue: The player is airborne and descending toward the ground while the crosshair remains on the copper golem.

steps.action: Before landing, left-click exactly once to strike the copper golem during the downward portion of the jump. Do not make a second attack. This is the report's critical-attack trigger.
steps.exact_input: Left-click once while descending and while the crosshair is on the copper golem
steps.success_cue: The single strike connects: the copper golem reacts to damage, and critical-hit particles should provide a visual confirmation that the intended attack type was executed. No additional attack has been made.

stor.handoff_condition: The fully charged, single descending melee strike has just connected with the copper golem. Immediately hand control to the observation subsystem to capture and classify the attack audio, without attacking again or changing sound settings.
uncertainties: The report does not specify single-player versus dedicated-server testing, a world seed, coordinates, difficulty, or an initial game mode. This plan uses a new single-player Creative world for setup and Survival mode for the critical attack because no server-specific condition is stated.

The report says to summon a copper golem but supplies no command. To avoid inventing an unverified command string, this plan uses the officially documented carved-pumpkin-on-copper-block construction method.

The report does not specify a weapon. An unenchanted Iron Sword is selected as a simple conventional melee weapon; it is a practical implementation choice and is not asserted as required by the report.
The report does not specify audio-volume settings, resource packs, or mods. Audible vanilla sound output is established only so the requested sound-triggering action can be evaluated reliably.

The exact critical-hit timing instructions are an operational reconstruction of the report's phrase "Critically attack". The trigger should be retried from step 10 only if the strike misses or no critical-hit particles appear; do not repeat successful strikes merely to amplify the behavior.
